newsitem.title: USA: Most IMM currencies end lower on Greenspan remarks.
newsitem.headline: Most IMM currencies end lower on Greenspan remarks.

text.p: Most IMM currencies finished lower after U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's remarks solidified market expectations for a U.S. rate hike at next Tuesday's FOMC meeting, traders and analysts said.
"The dollar started rallying before Greenspan's comments, and he certainly delivered," Dave Durrant, senior currency strategist at I.D.E.A. Inc, said.
Greenspan in prepared testimony to Congress said the U.S. must ideally act pre-emptively to keep inflation low, and said a further drop in joblessness would boost the risk of higher wages and prices.

While analysts believe currency futures will continue to fall ahead of the March 25 Federal Open Market Committee meeting, Durrant said the dollar's gains would be limited at 1.6950 marks and 124.10 yen in the interim.
Those cash levels correspond to $0.5932 in June marks and $0.008156 in June yen -- levels both contracts managed to hold above despite active fund and dealer selling in both pits, traders said.
Both contracts, plus June Swiss francs, steadily inched lower in the afternoon, but one technician said Swiss franc futures looked firmer technically.

"Swiss franc futures look a little better than marks because June once again rose above $0.6965, but I would say for the contract to turn around it would have to close above $0.7140," he said, referring to the 1-1/2-month high.
Resistance for June marks is at the 1-1/4-month high of $0.6037.

Some pit traders said June marks could hit that level on continued talk about a delay in the European Monetary Union start date. Earlier in the day, rumors circulated in the futures market that there would be an EMU announcement during Thursday's overnight GLOBEX session.
On Monday, German Finance Minister Theo Waigel was quoted in a daily German newspaper as saying that fulfilling the Maastricht criteria was more important than sticking to a strict timetable.
"The thing curbing the dollar's rally is talk of an EMU delay," Durrant said.

Durrant noted that anticipation the U.S. administration may jawbone the dollar lower was also undermining the dollar's upside momentum. The U.S. manufacturing sector could pressure the administration into forsaking its strong dollar policy, as U.S. exports fell in January.
According to the U.S. January trade report, U.S. exports fell 0.6 percent to $70.78 billion, from a downward revised $71.21 billion in December.

At the end of pit trade, June yen was off $0.000063 at $0.008180, marks were down $0.0038 at $0.5944, Swiss francs were off $0.0044 at $0.6948, sterling was off $0.0056 at $1.5914, Canadian dollars were off $0.0013 at $0.7293, Australian dollars were up $0.0002 at $0.7866 and Mexican pesos were up $0.000325 at $0.121450.
